title: Voltage is a difference
description: Voltage is a push between two points, not a stuff that sits in the wire. You measure it across, not through.

blocks.md:
## A push between two points

Voltage is a difference. Think of it as a height: high on one side of the battery, low on the other. Charge wants to fall from high to low if a path exists. The number on a cell — 1.5 V — is how big that difference is, not how much “electricity” is stored in the copper.

This bites when people say a wire “has voltage in it” the way a bottle has water. A single point does not have a useful voltage by itself. You always pick two points. Across the battery. Across the lamp. Never “through” a point as if voltage were a flow.

![Voltage is high versus low](assets/voltage-difference.svg)

```text
HIGH (+)  --push-->  LOW (−)
measure ACROSS two points
```

A common mistake is treating voltage as stuff in the wire, or as another word for current. The questions ask you to keep them apart.

choices.md: A difference — a push between two points
A stuff that lives inside the wire

blocks.explainMd: Voltage is across. Current is through. They are partners, not synonyms.

blocks.explainMd: V across. I through. That pairing is the whole measuring story later.
